# Recorded CLI fixtures

Sessions written by the real agent CLIs, one dir per version, read by `TestRecordedFixtures`. `scripts/record-fixtures.go` records them in a throwaway home against a local fake model: no account or paid inference; updates and telemetry disabled, paths replaced by `/work/proj` and `/home/user`, long strings (system prompts) cut, and a recording that still names the machine fails. Limits are pinned from a real response with every value replaced: `-codex-limits-from` (a Codex rollout) and `-claude-limits` (one call to Claude Code's usage endpoint with your login, keeping only the fields lazyagents reads).

Collected native settings are recorder inputs accepted by the CLI, not evidence of its defaults. OS/architecture missing from older recordings remain unknown. Resume arguments alone do not prove native resumption or deletion. Supplementary Linux/amd64 evidence below verifies headless Gemini/OpenCode resume and adapter backup/delete; interactive resume UIs and other versions/platforms remain outside those probes. Hermes has no runnable CLI recording yet (F05 in BACKLOG.md).

Gemini 0.64.0 usage goldens count durable response IDs once across repeated snapshots. OpenCode 2.0.32 usage goldens retain response provider/model, separate cache counters and authoritative recorded cost, including zero. Token/cost values in these local fake-model recordings are synthetic, not production billing.

To pin a new CLI release, install it and run `go run scripts/record-fixtures.go -only <agent>`, then `go test ./internal/agent -run TestRecordedFixtures -update`. Keep older versions: they are the matrix.

The recorder refuses existing version directories; use a separate `-out` directory to review a replacement. Gemini uses the native `--skip-trust` automation flag only in its empty temporary workspace; no persistent trust record is created.

Gemini 0.64.0 also retains `provider-roundtrip.json`: `-only gemini-cli -gemini-provider-roundtrip -out <temporary-directory>` verifies saved-token and fixed GEMINI_API_KEY GenerateContent apply/clear through the real CLI, with no endpoint/model/key flags masking persisted settings. The fake endpoint validates x-goog-api-key and native sessions record the expected applied/restored models. `TestRecordedGeminiProviderRoundTrip` replays those inputs. Original session fixtures stay retained; trust is supplied only by the native ephemeral --skip-trust flag inside an empty temporary workspace.

OpenCode 2.0.32 also retains `provider-roundtrip.json`: `-only opencode -opencode-provider-roundtrip -out <temporary-directory>` records token, environment-reference and keyless Chat Completions apply/clear with synthetic credentials. Each config is verified by native `run --standalone` and its recorded model; the original session fixture is retained. `TestRecordedOpenCodeProviderRoundTrip` replays those edits. A background service may cache old settings; reload/restart it before testing changed global settings. JSONC comments/trailing commas and multiple global files are not supported for provider writes.

Supplementary session evidence (original recordings retained):

- [Gemini 0.64.0 lifecycle](gemini-cli/0.64.0/session-lifecycle/origin.json): `-only gemini-cli -session-lifecycle -out <temporary-directory>`. Native headless `--resume` adds one user turn to the same ID; the adapter then makes an exact private file backup and deletes the original. `lifecycle.json` retains results; `home/` is the snapshot before deletion. `TestRecordedLifecycleProof` replays the resumed snapshot; `TestGeminiNativeClockIgnoresCopiedFileTime` verifies the original recording's clock independently of copied mtime. The reader renders each tool/message snapshot once and applies native resume content/order patches.
- [OpenCode 2.0.32 links/lifecycle](opencode/2.0.32/session-links/origin.json): `-only opencode -session-links -session-lifecycle -out <temporary-directory>`. Native `subagent` results record `metadata.sessionID`; read-only parent membership confirms the link. Headless `run --session` resumes the same parent; adapter deletion uses `session export --standalone` for the parent and every descendant before `session delete --standalone`. Each export must identify the requested session and contain its messages. The fixture snapshot precedes deletion; `lifecycle.json` records two private backups and no remaining V2 sessions.
- [Crush 0.98.1 links](crush/0.98.1/session-links/origin.json): `-only crush -session-links -out <temporary-directory>`. Native child IDs join the assistant message ID and tool-call ID with `$$`; the child's `parent_session_id` must also match. The native child tool set in this recording does not execute a shell command. `TestRecordedChildNavigation` replays parent/child goldens for both SQLite agents and refuses a child whose recorded parent changed. Absent or mismatched IDs leave the tool visible without a navigation link. No title/time matching is used.
